statements.statement: Town meeting passed the citizens' petition Prop 2.5 override by a narrow margin.
A member said last year's override already added to tax bills and a new one would add further.
A member proposed using free cash to help offset not doing the override this year.
A member reported the state's minimum per-pupil aid increase was raised.
Prior minimum new aid level before the increase was cited.
A preliminary cherry sheet figure was mentioned during discussion of state aid.
A member cited health insurance cost growth as a recurring budget pressure.
A member said the school budget faces roughly a one-million-dollar gap in the coming year.
The same member said the gap grows to about two million the following year if unaddressed.

warnings.condition: if the FY26 override is not passed in time
warnings.prediction: Staff layoffs are imminent and unemployment payouts will come out of the school budget.

warnings.condition: if action on the override is delayed
warnings.prediction: The district will lose good teachers permanently as they find other jobs during the delay.

warnings.condition: without a stable multi-year budget resolution
warnings.prediction: Continued budget uncertainty is harming morale and the district's ability to attract and retain quality staff.
A department requiring 12% annual growth against a 2.5% levy cap is not sustainable and something must change.

warnings.condition: if the multi-year deficits are not otherwise resolved
warnings.prediction: An override question is expected to be on the ballot again next year given both a near-term and a larger following-year deficit.
